title: Child poverty is a multidimensional deprivation shaped by household resources, services, social protection, and converging crises
source_unit: UNICEF, The State of the World's Children 2025: Ending Child Poverty: Our Shared Imperative
geography: Global child-poverty, deprivation, social-protection, climate, conflict, service, and public-finance evidence with low-, middle-, and high-income comparisons

denominator.unit: children globally assessed against the extreme monetary-poverty line

extreme_poverty_children.unit: million children living in extreme monetary poverty

poverty_line.unit: US dollars per person per day

relative_risk.value: children are more than twice as likely as adults to live in extreme monetary poverty

observations.method: UNICEF synthesis of global monetary-poverty estimates and child-focused analysis of household resources and rights.
observations.uncertainty: Monetary poverty is a threshold measure and does not fully capture in-kind services, intra-household allocation, temporary shocks, or multidimensional deprivation.
observations.subgroup: Young children, children with disabilities, rural and Indigenous children, displaced children, and children in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
observations.counterinterpretation: Income support, public services, social protection, and local conditions can reduce deprivation even when household monetary income remains low.

observations.period: 2025; multidimensional deprivation in low- and middle-income countries

denominator.unit: children in low- and middle-income countries assessed across vital deprivation domains

multiple_deprivation.value: more than one in five children are severely deprived in at least two vital areas

sanitation_low_income.unit: percent of children in low-income countries lacking access to a toilet

sanitation_lower_middle.unit: percent of children in lower-middle-income countries lacking access to a toilet

sanitation_upper_middle.unit: percent of children in upper-middle-income countries lacking access to a toilet

observations.method: UNICEF multidimensional child-poverty synthesis across housing, nutrition, water, sanitation, education, healthcare, and related rights.
observations.uncertainty: Domain thresholds and country coverage differ; deprivation counts do not establish identical severity, duration, or causal pathways for each child.
observations.subgroup: Children in low-income settings, rural communities, informal settlements, households without safe water or sanitation, and children facing barriers to schooling or healthcare.
observations.counterinterpretation: Progress in one service domain can materially improve child well-being even when other deprivations persist; averages can conceal local improvements and inequalities.

observations.period: 2025; social protection, informal work, and caregiver security

denominator.unit: children and working households assessed for social-protection and labor-market conditions

children_without_social_protection.unit: billion children globally lacking any social-protection coverage

informal_work.unit: percent of the global workforce in informal employment in 2023

african_working_poverty.unit: percent of working people in Africa living in poverty

policy_set.value: child benefits, public services, decent work, parental leave, and affordable childcare are identified as mutually reinforcing responses

observations.method: UNICEF synthesis linking child poverty to social-protection coverage, caregiver employment, informality, wages, leave, childcare, and public services.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage and labor indicators use different denominators and reference years; association with child outcomes does not establish the effect of one benefit or labor reform.
observations.subgroup: Children in working-poor households, informal workers, caregivers, women with care responsibilities, and families without parental leave or childcare.
observations.counterinterpretation: Informal work can provide income where formal employment is scarce, and targeted or universal benefits may work differently depending on take-up, adequacy, and delivery capacity.

observations.period: 2024-2030; climate, conflict, and funding risks to child well-being

denominator.unit: children and public systems exposed to converging climate, conflict, and financing risks

climate_hazard_exposure.unit: percent of children facing at least one extreme climate hazard each year

conflict_exposure.unit: percent of the world's children living in a conflict area in 2024

debt_service_health.unit: developing countries paying more in debt interest than they spend on health

debt_service_education.unit: developing countries paying more in debt interest than they spend on education

observations.method: UNICEF synthesis of child climate-risk, conflict, public-finance, aid, education, health, and social-protection evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The indicators describe exposure and fiscal conditions, not the same children or a single causal pathway; projections about aid cuts and mortality depend on policy responses and assumptions.
observations.subgroup: Children in climate-exposed, conflict-affected, displaced, indebted, and aid-dependent settings, plus communities relying on public health and education systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Climate-resilient services, debt restructuring, social protection, humanitarian access, and protected child spending can interrupt the compound-risk pathway.

related_sources.claim: UNICEF Learning Interrupted provides complementary evidence on climate-related school disruption.
UNICEF flagship report archive provides related child-trend publications and prior editions.

boundary: This record adds a child-poverty route linking monetary resources to sanitation, housing, nutrition, education, healthcare, social protection, caregiver work, climate hazards, conflict, debt, and public budgets. It uses publication-level aggregate evidence, not child-level panel histories, household spending microdata, respondent-level deprivation interviews, or causal estimates of any single service or fiscal policy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UNICEF State of the World's Children 2025 page was reviewed for monetary and multidimensional poverty, social protection, informal work, caregiver policy, climate, conflict, debt, and service-financing claims.
